Reviewing usRds

Source: REVIEWING.md

Shared standards for human, ChatGPT and Claude reviews. Read AGENTS.md too. This file grants no posting, implementation, approval or merge permission.

Policy revision and scope

For PR reviews, record the current target-branch SHA and read AGENTS.md and REVIEWING.md at that revision. Proposed policy changes are reviewed under the existing target policy, never their own proposed rules. For local reviews, use committed policy at HEAD and assess uncommitted policy edits separately. Implementation follows applicable working-branch and subdirectory guidance.

Begin with the reviewed copy, branch, exact commit, comparison scope and policy revision. GitHub excludes unpushed work. If a local folder is connected, inspect status, staged/unstaged diffs and relevant untracked source without modifying it. Otherwise use an isolated GitHub copy; verify the actual default branch.

A PR/branch is compared with its target using the merge base. A named commit or latest default-branch change is compared with its parent unless another scope is requested; identify the parent for a merge commit. Whole-package reviews cover the whole package. Follow-ups focus on changes since the previous reviewed revision, retain full relevant context, and do not repeat resolved findings. If history was rewritten, explain the revised comparison rather than assume the earlier head is an ancestor.

Procedure

  1. Establish intent from the PR, milestone, linked issues and durable design records. Distinguish verified defects, validation gaps, methodological choices, intentional unfinished work and unrelated existing limitations. Read changed human-written code and relevant surrounding paths; identify omitted or truncated material. Reserve whole-package coverage for an explicitly whole-package review.

  2. Trace downstream effects through callers, joins, returned objects and their attributes, tests, documentation and affected workflows. Evaluate whether a design fits existing APIs or duplicates functionality. Intentional, documented interface changes may be appropriate during development; accidental breakage is still a defect.

  3. Derive edge cases independently of the implementation. Verify scientific claims against release-appropriate authoritative sources. A missing source is an evidence gap, not proof that a definition is wrong. Do not silently settle an unresolved methodological choice.

  4. Evaluate tests and CI independently: passing checks can encode incorrect assumptions. Check expected values, mock boundaries, skips and whether a regression test detects the original bug. Inspect CI for the reviewed SHA; distinguish absent, pending, failed and passed checks. Do not equate a website build with a full package check.

  5. Execute only safe, relevant synthetic checks in isolation after the startup and data-access inspection required by AGENTS.md. Never run live tests. Missing checks and dependency limitations must be reported without claiming execution based on someone else’s report.

    Choose validation scope for each PR from the changed behavior and its downstream reach, not merely the number of changed lines. State the selected scope and rationale. Run focused checks first; expand when shared interfaces, scientific calculations, dependencies, or observed failures warrant it. Distinguish failures introduced by the PR from existing failures. If adequate validation is unavailable, report the specific gap. Do not expand into an unrelated whole-package audit.

  6. Reconcile previous findings against the current code and milestone. Identify partial fixes without repeating resolved findings or treating every open issue as a new regression. Assess other reviewers’ claims rather than automatically accepting them.

usRds-specific checks

  • Identifier types/precision, leading zeros, join keys and row multiplication; patient-, episode-, encounter-, claim- and revenue-line aggregation.
  • SAS/CSV/Parquet equivalence, column selection, dates and time units, file coverage and layouts across releases, duplicate format selection, partial years, cache scope and stale session state.
  • Variable-specific missing codes, labels versus underlying codes, and absent required columns. Package metadata and converted tables are not infallible scientific authorities.
  • ICD version and date applicability, code formatting, exact versus prefix matching, diagnosis/procedure positions and distinct-encounter rules.
  • Eligibility and coverage intervals, claims completeness versus administrative follow-up, event/censoring boundaries, retransplants, row-varying baselines, cohort attributes and finalization state.
  • Payment versus charge definitions, claim/revenue overlap, conservation under proration, partial windows, negative adjustments, missing values and inflation index direction/coverage. Preserve a named source for each monetary measure.
  • Installation, exports/imports, dependency declarations, generated help consistency and affected vignettes. Check Windows paths, encoding, case, locale and line endings when relevant.
  • Data provenance, live-test guards, permitted write destinations and the maintainer-only regeneration rule. Report uncertain data by path only; distinguish suspected exposure from established exposure.

Reporting

Group actionable findings as Must fix, Should fix, or Consider, omitting empty groups. Prioritize incorrect calculations, silent corruption, broken installation/exports, unsafe data access and misleading claims. Development stage does not excuse these. Documented unfinished work may be acceptable for its milestone but must not be represented as complete or ready to merge. Missing documentation or validation has severity proportional to its impact, not an automatic severity solely from the file type.

For each finding give file and line, classification (verified defect, validation gap or methodological decision), problem, practical impact and suggested fix. Use focused snippets when helpful. Avoid stylistic nitpicks and unnecessary arguments, abstractions or process. Missing generated help can be noted once as unfinished work; a broken export or installation retains its actual severity.

Separate source inspection, personally executed synthetic checks (commands and results), observed CI, author-reported validation and remaining real-data validation. Synthetic checks establish code behavior, not validity on real USRDS files. Provide exact maintainer validation commands when applicable, including relevant vignette rebuilding. List material reference/runtime/coverage limitations. Never reproduce private conversations or patient data.

End with a one-line verdict scoped to the reviewed changes. No findings does not imply formal approval, comprehensive correctness or real-data validation.
